name: Skeleton
summary: A greyed placeholder that holds a component's shape while its content loads.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-skeleton> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens; `variant` picks the shape (text / title / button / avatar) and the shimmer is an opacity PULSE (no gradient fill, per the no-gradient rule). Zero drift.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin attribute wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. Defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

spec.label: Motion
spec.value: opacity pulse 1.6s (respects reduced-motion); active=false stops it

whenToUse.when: content is loading and you want to hold its exact layout to avoid a jump
a short, indeterminate wait where the final shape is unknown

opinion.note: Match the skeleton to the real content's shape and size so nothing shifts when it resolves. Use it for the first load of a region; don't stack many pulsing blocks for a sub-second wait — a Spin is calmer.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — DS V3 has no measured Skeleton cell; spec derived from the token layer (fill gray-30, radius-xs) and antd Skeleton conventions (text/title/avatar shapes). Shimmer is an opacity pulse, not a gradient, to honour the no-gradient-on-fills rule. A deliberate, documented extension.

snippets.label: HTML
snippets.note: The native form — a web component in an HTML file renders on open, no build step.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Leaf = ONE shared element, single render.
